newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar edges lower with NY correction.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar edges lower with NY correction.

text.p: White sugar futures eased their way lower on Monday following the expected downward correction in New York but activity was generally subdued with only the two front contracts recording trades.
New York's March raws contract closed 27 points higher on Friday at 10.73 cents/lb and London traders said they expected a rapid correction lower. The position opened at 10.64 cents/lb.
A crossed trade of 280 lots on the spot March contract was the dominant feature of the day's activity and the white/raw premium also drew attention as it moved a touch higher to hover around $68.
"There's not much there to be excited about," a trader said.
At 1643 GMT March was down $1.90 at $301.50, just 30 cents off its intraday low. May was down $1.60 at the same level.
Overall volume reached a light 762 lots.
The London market was reluctant to show much of a reaction to recent physical news from Pakistan and Iraq as the reported developments had been widely expected.
Iraq tendered to buy between four and six cargoes of 100 ICUMSA white sugar on Tuesday for February/March shipment as part of the U.N. oil-for-food deal.
Pakistan's TCP buying agency scrapped its tender to buy 50,000 tonnes of crystal white sugar and reinvited bids for January delivery.
Trading was very quiet in Paris with just 101 lots on the board. March and May were both down by $1.50 and stood at $302.50 and $302.00 respectively.
